title: Signing the Zscaler Terraform providers in: OneAPI, legacy credentials and clouds

prose.text: The provider arguments themselves (including that `client_secret` conflicts with `private_key`) are generated: `node scripts/kb.mjs surface provider:zia` and the same for zpa, zcc and ztc. {{hardcoding-warning}}

prose.label: ZIA.
prose.text: {{zia-oneapi}} {{zia-env-vars}} {{zia-cloud-values}} Legacy mode, government clouds and sandbox credentials are in [[zia.terraform.provider-modes]].

prose.label: ZPA, ZCC and Cloud Connector.
prose.text: ZPA credentials, environment variables and cloud values are in [[zpa.terraform.provider-config]]; ZCC in [[zcc.terraform.provider-config]]; ZTC in [[cloud-connector.terraform.provider-behavior]].

prose.label: Underneath.
prose.text: How the SDK obtains and renews the OneAPI token is in [[shared.sdk-go.auth-lifecycle]], and what happens to secrets once Terraform holds them in [[shared.terraform.credential-handling]].

checks.do: Whether credentials come from environment variables rather than the configuration, since every provider's documentation warns against hard-coding them.
Whether zscaler_cloud is set only for a non-production environment (beta, gov, govus).

hardcoding-warning.statement: The ZIA, ZPA, ZCC and ZTC provider documentation each warn that hard-coding credentials into a Terraform configuration is not recommended and risks secret leakage if the file is committed to public version control.

quotes: Hard-coding credentials into any Terraform configuration is not recommended, and risks secret leakage should this file be committed to public version control
evidence.after: **NOTE**: The `zscaler_cloud` is optional for production comercial Clouds

zia-oneapi.statement: From v4.0.0 the ZIA provider supports authentication through OneAPI, which uses the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow: the client exchanges its credentials for an access token, with no user authentication involved.

quotes: Zscaler OneAPI uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework
As of version v4.0.0, this provider supports authentication via the new Zscaler API framework
OneAPI uses the Client Credentials OAuth flow, in which client applications can exchange their credentials with the authorization server for an access token
without any user authentication involved in the process.

zia-env-vars.statement: The ZIA provider documentation maps `client_id`, `client_secret`, the private key, `vanity_domain` and `zscaler_cloud` to `ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID`, `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY`, `ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN` and `ZSCALER_CLOUD`, and says a setting supplied by environment variable need not be set in the provider block.

quotes: | `client_id`     | _(String)_ Zscaler API Client ID, used with `clientSecret` or `PrivateKey` OAuth auth mode.         | `ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID`      |
| `client_secret` | _(String)_ Secret key associated with the API Client ID for authentication.                         | `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET`  |
| `vanity_domain` | _(String)_ Refers to the domain name used by your organization.                                     | `ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN`  |
| `zscaler_cloud`         | _(String)_ The name of the Zidentity cloud, e.g., beta.                                             | `ZSCALER_CLOUD`          |
If environment variables are utilized for provider settings the
corresponding variable name does not need to be set in the provider config
evidence.after: # Configure the ZIA Provider (OneAPI Authentication) - Private Key

zia-cloud-values.statement: For the ZIA provider, `zscaler_cloud` is optional for production commercial clouds and only required for other environments: `beta` for the test commercial cloud, and `gov` or `govus` for FedRAMP.

quotes: **NOTE**: The `zscaler_cloud` is optional for production comercial Clouds and ONLY required when authenticating to other environments.
